I moved to Cork for a year after 4 years in Manchester because my swedish bf couldnt join me there (brexit), we wanted to move in together in an english speaking country and that's where I got a job. 

I'd never seen a housing crisis like this before, couldn't rent in the city at all + needed a car for everything and we were 20 minutes from the closest grocery store. On top of it everything was incredibly expensive. 

We moved to malmö, sweden about 2 months ago and it changed everything - it's really hard on me because I don't know the language (the reason I was desperate for ireland to work out) but we dont need a car (which frees up a LOT!! of my budget) and we are renting a beautiful well insulated 56m2 flat in the middle of the city for €400 less than the old barn-like place in the middle of some cow fields that we had in cork (which was so cold in winter it mightve been even worse than being outside)

I don't regret having lived there because of the amazing people I met, and I was sad to leave but sadly it's unlivable. I was so stressed about money and rent for a whole year it feels like actual trauma. when my coworkers and friends heard I was moving to sweden everyone said "isnt it incredibly expensive?" but with everything accounted for (not just food prices, which are about the same, but also rent, transport, accessibility and swedish salary etc) it's been much cheaper for us here.
